slides.title: A pattern with a power gap
slides.text: Cyberbullying is not one cross message. It is a pattern: repeated harm, aimed at someone who cannot easily make it stop. That power gap is what makes it bullying.
slides.alt: Would you rather put class work on a page anyone can comment on, or a page only your class can see?

focus.cue: A page where anyone can pile in
Only your class can comment here

slides.title: Drama is different
slides.text: Digital drama is conflict that escalates online: friends fall out, screenshots fly, and an audience piles in. Drama involves equals. Bullying involves a gap, and the response differs.
slides.alt: Would you rather delete an old post you are embarrassed by, or leave it up and laugh about it?

focus.cue: Delete it, and the drama loses its fuel
Leave it, and the audience keeps it alive

slides.title: Four roles in the round
slides.text: Every incident has roles: the target, the actor, the bystanders and the upstander. Most people are bystanders, which is exactly why bystanders decide how these stories end.
slides.alt: A second online dilemma: posting your work brings feedback, and can also show more than you meant.

focus.cue: Your words, inside the chat for now
A copy outside it, beyond your control

slides.title: Hate speech: report, don't debate
slides.text: Hate speech attacks who someone is, and it crosses a line no joke can excuse. The Defender move is never to debate it. Save it, report it, and support the person it targeted.
slides.alt: A real message for once: your teacher, a sender you know, about the field trip forms. Nothing to tap, no rush.

focus.cue: Evidence first: a message you can save and show
Read carefully, then report: never debate it

slides.title: The bystander move
slides.text: A mocking post about a classmate is gathering laughs in a group chat. Rank the bystander moves by the good they do.
steps: Weakest: laugh along and add a joke
Passive: read it and say nothing
Strong: a kind word to the target
Strongest: save it, report it, back the target
slides.alt: Would you rather put class work on a page anyone can comment on, or a page only your class can see?

focus.cue: Laugh along, and the pile-on grows
A kind word to the target changes the ending

slides.title: Evidence, reporting, repair
slides.text: Keep the evidence, use the report tools, and tell a trusted adult; serious harassment can be a legal matter for adults to handle. If you were the actor: stop, delete, apologize, and accept the consequences.
slides.alt: Spot the trick, Pro style: the lesson card names the levers. Rush, prizes, and asking for your mailbox key.

focus.cue: Spot the trick: the chapter that trains your eye
Rush, prizes, key asks, strangers: the evidence list

words.means: repeated online harm aimed at someone who cannot easily stop it
conflict between equals that escalates online
a bystander who acts to help the target
words attacking who someone is, to be reported, not debated

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Play Would You Rather: choose the Online topic and play Online: share or keep. Your teacher may lead this one; know your school reporting route before you start.
slides.alt: An online dilemma in Pro: make it public and be found, or keep it private and stay safe — a real tradeoff.

focus.cue: Play Online: share or keep, and judge each pair
